claims.text: The starting material is the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
A heterogeneous grain structure containing nanoscale precipitates can be introduced into HfZrTiTa0.53.
The nanoscale precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates will promote strain hardening.
The heterogeneous grain structure with nanoscale precipitates will improve uniform deformability.
The heterogeneous grain structure with nanoscale precipitates will reduce the likelihood of rapid failure during adiabatic dynamic deformation.
The intervention will increase yield strength by 10–20% relative to the stated quasi-static baseline.
The intervention will increase compressive strength by 15–30% relative to the stated quasi-static baseline.
The intervention will increase fracture strain by 20–40% relative to the stated quasi-static baseline.
The predicted improvements apply under adiabatic dynamic deformation at strain rates from 10^2 to 10^4 s^-1.
The predicted improvements apply at temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The magnitude of the improvements may depend on processing conditions and microstructural characteristics.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing otherwise matched HfZrTiTa0.53 specimens with and without the heterogeneous grain structure and nanoscale precipitates under adiabatic dynamic deformation.
Yield strength, compressive strength, fracture strain, and microstructure will be measured in the comparison.
